title: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2006 (Cth)
status: In Force (applies to life insurers for designated life and sinking fund policies only)
licence: Commonwealth of Australia, CC BY 4.0 (legislation.gov.au). Paraphrased; consult the authorised compilation.
verification_notes: Section 5 definition of life policy and s6 table 1 items 37 to 39 read from compilation dated 1 October 2026 (latest on 2026-10-19). Life policy excludes policies with no prescribed minimum surrender value, regular premium policies of 1,500 dollars a year or less, single premium policies of 3,000 dollars or less (or higher amounts in the AML/CTF Rules), and consumer credit insurance. General insurance and private health insurance are not designated services in table 1 (from reading the insurance references in the compilation; an SME should confirm no other item captures insurer activity). AUSTRAC states the 2024 reform obligations apply to existing reporting entities from 31 March 2026 and to new Tranche 2 sectors from 1 July 2026 (from AUSTRAC pages via search). The 13 December 2006 assent date is from general knowledge.
summary: The AML/CTF Act requires reporting entities providing designated services to enrol with AUSTRAC, maintain an AML/CTF program, conduct customer due diligence, monitor and report suspicious matters and keep records. For insurers, the designated services are issuing or undertaking liability under, accepting premiums for, and making payments under life policies (as defined, broadly investment-style policies with a surrender value above small premium thresholds) and sinking fund policies. Risk-only life cover, general insurance and private health insurance are generally outside the regime. The 2024 reforms changed program and due diligence obligations from 31 March 2026.

clauses.heading: Life policy and sinking fund policy designated services
clauses.text: Issuing or undertaking liability as insurer under a life policy or sinking fund policy (item 37), accepting a premium for one (item 38) and making a payment under one (item 39) are designated services, so a life insurer providing them is a reporting entity. 'Life policy' excludes policies without a prescribed minimum surrender value, small regular or single premium policies and consumer credit insurance (s5).
subclauses: Item 37 Issuing or undertaking liability under a life or sinking fund policy (customer: policyholder).
Item 39 Making a payment under the policy (customer: payee).
s5 life policy exclusions: no minimum surrender value; regular premiums up to 1,500 dollars a year; single premium up to 3,000 dollars; consumer credit insurance.
clauses.notes: Reference only. Relevant if an AI agent onboards customers or pays surrender or maturity values on investment-linked life policies.
